title: Production monitoring
prompt: A product-return model is running in production, but the true outcomes arrive weeks later. What could you monitor immediately, and how would you check later whether predictive performance has changed?
objective: Distinguish early production signals from direct performance measurement after outcomes arrive.
expected_scope: Name an immediate signal and baseline, then describe a later labelled evaluation.
hint: Which measurements are possible before you know whether the predicted event happened?
reference_explanation: Compare input distributions or missing-value rates with a reference period to flag changes. A shift is a signal to investigate, because a changed input mix can leave accuracy unchanged. When outcomes arrive, match them to the original predictions and compare a relevant metric, such as return-class recall, to its baseline over a comparable window.

criteria.description: Names a measurable immediate signal and an appropriate reference baseline.
Explains why a distribution change alone does not establish worse predictions.
Explains using later outcomes matched to past predictions to calculate and compare a relevant quality metric.

critical_misconceptions: Concluding that prediction accuracy has dropped based solely on a change in input distributions.
